settings.content:
Immunoglobulins, also known as antibodies, are proteins produced by your immune system that help protect your body from harmful invaders like bacteria, viruses, and toxins. Normally, pathogens have the potential to trigger the immune system if they pass through a damaged gut lining (aka a leaky gut).

Immunoglobulins help to protect your gut barrier by binding and neutralizing toxic microbial antigens, while not harming any of the good bacteria in your gut. The immunoglobulin in Tribiotic is non systemic and works locally in the GI tract to help support digestion and immune function.

settings.content:
While most probiotics simply add beneficial bacteria, Tribiotic takes a more advanced approach to gut, vaginal, and immune health by combining prebiotics, probiotics, postbiotics, and a potent immunoglobulin.

One of the key issues with many probiotics on the market is their lack of stability, what’s in the capsule may not actually survive long enough to be effectively delivered to your gut. That means you could be getting fewer benefits than promised.

Tribiotic overcomes this by including stable, clinically studied strains of probiotics, along with prebiotics to fuel their growth and postbiotics, which are already in their most active, stable form, so you know you’re getting real results.

What truly sets Tribiotic apart is the addition of immunoglobulin. This powerful protein not only neutralizes harmful toxins and bad bacteria in your gut but also strengthens your gut barrier, helping to prevent harmful substances from leaking into your bloodstream.

By supporting the gut barrier and detoxifying your system, Tribiotic creates the optimal environment for beneficial bacteria to thrive.
settings.title: How is this different from other probiotics?

settings.content: Prebiotics are fibers that feed the probiotics (good bacteria) in your gut, helping them grow and thrive. By supporting the growth of probiotics, prebiotics play a key role in maintaining a balanced and healthy microbiome.
settings.title: How do prebiotics support probiotics?

settings.content: Probiotics are beneficial bacteria that live in your gut and help maintain a balanced microbiome. They support digestion, boost immune function, and promote overall gut health by keeping harmful bacteria in check.
settings.title: What are probiotics?
